requirement:
Every `habeas author` form MUST assess its subjects under an assessment policy,
`confirm` or `once`. The policy MUST come from `--policy <name>` when given,
otherwise from the selected configuration's `policy`, and otherwise MUST be
`once` for OpenAI and `confirm` for other backends. Under `confirm`, each subject MUST be assessed as
{cite}`requirements.authoring.confirmation` specifies. Under `once`, each subject
MUST receive a single assessment (including model escalation under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.adaptive`), whose result is recorded; it uses fewer tokens
and less time, such as with a slow local model. An unknown policy name MUST be
rejected as invalid configuration or arguments. The completion report MUST name
the policy used, and each usage record MUST identify it.
rationale:
## Obligations and implementation

- **Every author form assesses under `confirm` or `once`.** `src/config.rs#enum[AssessmentPolicy]` restricts the policy to these alternatives. `src/main.rs#fn[main]` passes the selected policy to single-subject and batch authoring; `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_assessment]` and `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[run_batch]` resolve it before assessment. The policy tests in `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[policy_comes_from_the_flag_then_the_configuration_then_defaults_to_confirm]` exercise single-subject, stdout, and batch invocation.
- **An explicit flag wins; otherwise the selected configuration wins; otherwise OpenAI uses `once`; otherwise other backends use `confirm`.** All four obligations are implemented by `src/config.rs#impl[ResolvedAuthoringConfig]/fn[effective_policy]`. They are tested by `tests/configuration.rs#fn[authoring_policy_defaults_to_confirm_and_round_trips]` and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_policy_defaults_to_once_without_changing_explicit_policy]`, with CLI precedence also tested by the batch-file policy test above.
- **`confirm` applies `requirements.authoring.confirmation`.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[assess_subject]` selects confirmation rather than returning the first favorable assessment. The adaptive equivalent is reachable through `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_record]` at `src/authoring/adaptive.rs#fn[assess]`. Selection is tested by `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[confirm_with_all_runs_a_second_assessment_for_each_batch_subject]` and the two policy-marked adaptive tests in `tests/authoring_cli.rs`.
- **`once` performs one assessment, including adaptive escalation; its result is recorded.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[assess_subject]` returns the first assessment under `once`; `src/authoring/adaptive.rs#fn[assess]` similarly returns the routed assessment, whose escalation is implemented by `fn[route]`. `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_assessment]` writes the resulting record. The CLI policy test checks conversation counts and stdout determination; `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[adaptive_routes_fresh_assessments_and_records_each_model]` and `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[adaptive_sol_failure_is_final_and_confirm_uses_sol_verification]` check routed attempts and recorded results.
- **Unknown policy names are rejected as arguments; unknown configuration policy names are rejected.** `src/config.rs#impl[AssessmentPolicy/std::str::FromStr]/fn[from_str]` and the deserialized `AssessmentPolicy` enum implement these separately. Both rejection routes are asserted by the CLI policy test and configuration round-trip test above.
- **The completion report names the policy.** `src/main.rs#fn[main]` includes it in batch summaries and single-subject reports, including the stderr report for stdout evidence. All these output paths are asserted by the CLI policy test.
- **Every usage record identifies the policy.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_record]` sets it and `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[followup_log]` copies it into subsequent conversations, including adaptive attempts. The CLI policy test asserts policy values in ordinary first and confirmation usage records.

## Unacknowledged testing gap

The last obligation lacks an outcome assertion for the separate adaptive usage-record paths. `src/authoring/adaptive.rs#fn[attempt]` creates real-model attempt records through `followup_log`; `src/authoring/adaptive.rs#fn[assess]` also creates adaptive confirmation and verification records. The subject-marked tests `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[adaptive_routes_fresh_assessments_and_records_each_model]` and `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[adaptive_sol_failure_is_final_and_confirm_uses_sol_verification]` exercise these paths, but neither asserts that these records identify the selected policy. The former reads the logs and checks models, links, counts, and routing reasons, not their policy fields; the latter does not inspect those usage fields either. Inspection of the supplied subject-marked tests and a search of their files found no adaptive policy-field assertion.

This is an explicit presence obligation, so unchanged propagation through `followup_log` does not exempt it from testing. These tests already set up the provider and state directories, so no external-service or process-state exemption applies. No supplied FIXME acknowledges this gap.

text: :::{req} policy
Every `habeas author` form MUST assess its subjects under an assessment policy,
`confirm` or `once`. The policy MUST come from `--policy <name>` when given,
otherwise from the selected configuration's `policy`, and otherwise MUST be
`once` for OpenAI and `confirm` for other backends. Under `confirm`, each subject MUST be assessed as
{cite}`requirements.authoring.confirmation` specifies. Under `once`, each subject
MUST receive a single assessment (including model escalation under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.adaptive`), whose result is recorded; it uses fewer tokens
and less time, such as with a slow local model. An unknown policy name MUST be
rejected as invalid configuration or arguments. The completion report MUST name
the policy used, and each usage record MUST identify it.
:::{req} confirmation
Under the `confirm` policy of {cite}`requirements.authoring.policy`, authoring
MUST assess each subject in an independent second conversation whenever the
first assessment's determination is `true` or FIXME. The assessments agree when
their outcomes are the same kind; then the first assessment MUST be recorded.
When they disagree, the harness MUST verify the less favorable assessment, where
`false` is less favorable than FIXME and FIXME than `true`, in a third
independent conversation under {cite}`requirements.authoring.verifier_prompt`,
and record the outcome {cite}`requirements.authoring.verifier_outcome` derives.
For a site review, assessments that differ only in `applies` MUST also count as
disagreeing, the one with `applies` true being less favorable. The recorded
rationale MUST state that the assessments disagreed and what the verification
concluded, so the disagreement remains visible for review under
{cite}`requirements.cli.flip_guidance`. Each conversation MUST have its own
usage record. Citation reviews under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` and site reviews under
{cite}`requirements.references.site_review` that a command selects MUST be
confirmed in the same way, with the review's target as the subject.
:::{req} adaptive
Adaptive is experimental and requires explicit opt-in. For the OpenAI backend,
`model = "adaptive"` MUST select models locally rather
than send `adaptive` to the API. An assessment with an applicable existing
FIXME reference MUST go directly to `gpt-6.1-sol`. Otherwise it MUST begin with
`gpt-5.4-mini`: a true judgment is accepted, while false, FIXME, or a failed
conversation/submission MUST trigger one fresh Sol assessment. Sol's result
MUST be final for that assessment, including a false judgment or failure.
Provider errors, cancellation, mandatory-input failures, connection failures,
and usage-storage failures MUST NOT trigger model escalation.
Applicable FIXMEs MUST follow the subject's existing scope rules: requirement
references outside its own distributed sites, or the reviewed site's own FIXMEs.
Citation reviews have no applicable acknowledgments. Matching a literal word
inside unrelated text MUST NOT trigger pre-escalation.
Both tiers MUST inherit the selected credentials, endpoint, and inference
options. Explicit concrete model IDs MUST bypass adaptive routing. Each actual
model attempt MUST have a separate usage record with its real model name;
the adaptive record MUST link its attempts and record any routing reason.
Escalation MUST NOT persist intermediate mini evidence or pass mini's rationale
to Sol. Under explicit `confirm`, each independent assessment MUST use adaptive
routing; disagreements MUST be verified by Sol using the existing confirmation
selection rules. Adaptive routing MUST NOT perform sampled audits.
